text:
alex: Heads-up: a couple of onboarding sample apps started failing after we published 1.5.2. Vercel previews show `TypeError: fetch is not a function` inside our auth retry.

maria: hmm, did we change the exports map? I remember a small tidy that made ESM the primary target.

ty: checked the tarball: package.json exports only had an `import` target for `.` and removed the `require` target. Node/CJS consumers and some bundlers end up on a fallback that doesn't include our runtime adapters. Also TS can't find types: `Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood/inference-js'`.

alex: repro with sample: `npx create-redwood-sample && npm i @redwood/inference-js@1.5.2 && vercel dev` — fails in preview. Forcing CJS `require('./dist/index.cjs')` locally works.

maria: quick mitigation: add back conditional exports for `require`, include `./package.json` in exports, and add top-level `types` pointing at `dist/index.d.ts`. Example: `".": {"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs","default":"./dist/index.cjs"}`.

ty: runtime tweak too: change strict `if (typeof fetch !== 'function') throw` to a lazy adapter `const _fetch = globalThis.fetch ?? (() => { try { return require('node-fetch'); } catch { return undefined } })();` and only error if still undefined. That avoids false negatives in edge bundlers.

ci-bot: CI started for branch fix/exports-1.5.3.

maria: I'll open a tiny PR and cut 1.5.3 patch if CI looks green. Also add a release-note: "Fix: restore CJS entry & typings to avoid edge/bundler import regressions." Add a smoke test in sample CI that runs a lightweight Vercel/Cloudflare import check.

alex: thanks — ping me once the patch is published so we can update sample pins.
